name: Chartnote
description: Chartnote is an EHR-agnostic AI medical scribe that started as a template and dictation tool before adding AI capabilities. The free Basic plan includes 15 minutes dictation + 15 AI note credits/month. Premium runs $49/month for part-time use, while Max costs $99/month with 300 AI Scribe credits. Key differentiator: extensive smart templates and medical snippets (dot phrases) for structured documentation. Pay-as-you-go AI credits available without subscription. HIPAA compliant with 256-bit AES encryption. Honest assessment: the UX feels older than newer AI-native scribes, and AI is bolted onto a pre-existing template platform rather than being core. Best for clinicians already using Chartnote templates who want to add ambient AI.

faqs.q: How much does Chartnote cost in 2026?
faqs.a: Chartnote offers a free Basic plan (15 AI note credits/month), Premium at $49/month (100 credits), Max at $99/month (300 credits), and Team at $99.99/user/month. Pay-as-you-go AI credits available without subscription.

faqs.q: Does Chartnote have a free tier?
faqs.a: Yes. The Basic plan is free forever with 15 minutes dictation and 15 AI note credits per month. Enough to test the platform before committing to a paid plan.

faqs.q: Does Chartnote integrate with my EHR?
faqs.a: Chartnote is EHR-agnostic—it works with any EHR via copy-paste. There's no native API integration, so you'll copy generated notes into your system. This flexibility means it works everywhere but adds a manual step.

faqs.q: Is Chartnote good for mental health?
faqs.a: Not specifically. Chartnote was designed for general medical documentation, not therapy or psychiatry. Mental health clinicians should use purpose-built tools like Mentalyc ($20-70/mo), Upheal ($69/mo), or Freed ($39-119/mo).

faqs.q: Chartnote vs Freed: which is better?
faqs.a: Freed ($39-119/mo unlimited) is newer, AI-native, and offers unlimited notes. Chartnote ($49-99/mo capped) has stronger template/snippet features for structured documentation. Freed has modern UX; Chartnote feels older but more customizable for templates.
